issues.failure_explanation: For nondegenerate noisy data, the right-hand side averages over the random variable u_0, while the left-hand side is a pointwise function of u_0. The appendix's asserted equality between a pointwise log-density and its expectation is likewise false. Jensen's inequality instead bounds the expected conditional negative log-likelihood.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Put an expectation over p(u_0|a) on the left throughout the VLB derivation and consistently describe the objective as expected conditional negative log-likelihood.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed interpretation of the decomposed objective as a pointwise conditional-likelihood VLB is invalid in the noisy-data regime, although the averaged training objective remains meaningful.
issues.title: Conditional VLB confuses pointwise and expected log-likelihood
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the likelihood quantifier that preserves the decomposition and training objective.

issues.title: Reverse covariance rule does not cover general Gaussian observation noise
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised unknown-covariance regime requires a nontrivial covariance model and revised derivation; the alternative materially narrows the noisy-data justification.

Suppose that the initial state $u_0$ follows a Dirac distribution at a point $u_0$, i.e., $u_0 \sim \delta_{u_0}$

issues.failure_explanation: At t=1, u_{t-1}=u_0 is Dirac. It has no Lebesgue density of the kind used in the paper's entropy definition, and its differential entropy and the relevant conditional entropy are not finite quantities. Consequently, the proposition is not well-defined over its stated range t=1,...,T.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the proposition to t=2,...,T and treat the degenerate final step separately, or introduce a rigorous generalized-entropy formulation for singular measures.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition and its entropy-based covariance justification do not cover the final reverse step t=1 as claimed.
issues.title: Entropy proposition includes a degenerate case outside its density-based definitions
issues.why_classification: Restricting the time range is a short local repair and leaves the nondegenerate transitions intact.

where $\beta_t$ is the variance schedule such that the final state $u_T$ is approximately standard normal for $T$ sufficiently large.

issues.failure_explanation: Equality of the separate entropies of p and q does not imply q=p or that q attains the true data likelihood; Gaussian conditional entropy depends only on covariance and is unchanged by an incorrect learned mean. In the noise-free case even the displayed entropy equality generally fails because p(u_T|u_0) has covariance (1-bar-alpha_T)I, whereas q(u_T) is standard normal, with equality only in the unattained exact limit bar-alpha_T=0.
